questions.question: Which yellow boomerang is secretly a botanical berry wearing a fruit-pop-star costume?
questions.note: By botanical definition, bananas are true berries.

questions.question: Which red freckled picnic icon is fake-berry royalty in disguise?
questions.note: Strawberries are aggregate accessory fruits, not true berries.

questions.question: Which brainy sea noodle runs on a triple-heart plumbing system?
questions.note: Octopuses have three hearts: two for gills, one for the body.

questions.question: Which marsupial manufactures cube poop like tiny non-rollable dice?
questions.note: Wombat intestines shape feces into cubes.

questions.question: Which pantry goo can survive centuries and still be snack-compatible?
questions.note: Low water activity and acidity help honey resist spoilage.

questions.question: Which magical horse is an official national animal in the real world?
questions.note: The unicorn is the national animal of Scotland.

questions.question: Which smiling aquarium goblin can regrow limbs like save-scumming biology?
questions.note: Axolotls can regenerate limbs and some organs.

questions.question: Which sea floof holds hands while napping so the ocean does not kidnap friends?
questions.note: Sea otters often hold paws while resting in rafts.

questions.question: Which iron lace tower subtly grows taller when summer cranks the thermostat?
questions.note: Thermal expansion can increase its height by several centimeters.

questions.question: Which planet spins so lazily its day outlasts its year?
questions.note: One Venus rotation takes longer than one Venus orbit.

questions.question: Which Egyptian queen is chronologically closer to moon boots than pyramid builders?
questions.note: Cleopatra lived much later than the Great Pyramid era.

questions.question: Which war ended before a long coffee order could be prepared?
questions.note: It lasted about 38 to 45 minutes in 1896.

questions.question: Which lunchbox
is botanically a bean cousin?
questions.note: Peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts.

questions.question: Which fancy snack
is technically a seed dangling off a fake fruit?
questions.note: The edible cashew is the seed attached to the cashew apple.

questions.question: Which spiky tropical fruit makes farmers wait roughly two years for payoff?
questions.note: Pineapples often take around 18 to 24 months to mature.

questions.question: Which fluffy pet has a one-way digestive storyline with no vomit chapter?
questions.note: Rabbits cannot vomit because of digestive anatomy.

questions.question: Which predators were already old news before Earth had trees?
questions.note: Shark ancestors predate trees by tens of millions of years.

questions.question: Which jelly can reverse life stage like it found the biological undo button?
questions.note: It can revert from medusa stage back to polyp under stress.

questions.question: Which egg-laying mammal glows cyan under ultraviolet rave lighting?
questions.note: Platypus fur shows biofluorescence under UV light.

questions.question: Which eucalyptus nap specialist has fingerprints suspiciously close to ours?
questions.note: Koala fingerprints can resemble human fingerprints.

questions.question: Which skyscraper-neck mammal still has only seven neck vertebrae like humans?
questions.note: Both giraffes and humans have seven neck vertebrae.

questions.question: Which ocean titan has arteries so large they sound architecturally unreasonable?
questions.note: Blue whales have the largest known hearts and major blood vessels.

questions.question: Which chill tree-hanger risks everything once a week for a bathroom trip?
questions.note: Many sloths descend to the ground to defecate about weekly.

questions.question: Which fluttering flower visitor tastes with its feet first and asks questions later?
questions.note: Butterflies have taste receptors on their feet.

questions.question: Where does a cricket keep its ears if not near its tiny face?
questions.note: Crickets hear with tympanal organs on their forelegs.

questions.question: Which burger-side sauce was once pitched as stomach medicine?
questions.note: Nineteenth-century ketchup was marketed with medicinal claims.

questions.question: Which famous university started teaching before the Aztec Empire existed?
questions.note: Oxford teaching began centuries before the Aztec Empire.

questions.question: What limitation made one early alarm clock a very stubborn roommate?
questions.answer: It rang at only one fixed time
questions.note: Levi Hutchins built a clock in 1787 set only for 4:00 a.m.

questions.question: Which US state is both east-most and west-most because maps are weird?
questions.note: Aleutian islands cross the 180th meridian, creating both extremes.

questions.question: Which gas giant may host diamond rain in its deep pressure-cooker atmosphere?
questions.note: Models suggest carbon may compress into diamond in deep layers.

questions.question: Which bird can micro-sleep while still gliding over ocean highways?
questions.note: Frigatebirds can sleep briefly during long flights.

questions.question: Which fearless mammal can shrug off venom doses that wreck larger animals?
questions.note: Honey badgers show resistance to some venoms.

questions.question: Which reptiles can winter-breathe through their rear plumbing under ice?
questions.note: Certain turtles use cloacal respiration in low-oxygen winter conditions.

questions.question: Which fish can identify human faces like a tiny wet bouncer?
questions.note: Archerfish have shown human-face discrimination in experiments.

questions.question: Which urban birds once worked as flying camera drones before drones were cool?
questions.note: Pigeon-mounted cameras were used in early aerial photography.

questions.question: Which country keeps an official approved baby-name list for parents?
questions.note: Iceland has naming rules and an approved register system.

questions.question: Which mammal runs blood pressure settings that would terrify your doctor?
questions.note: Giraffes need very high pressure to move blood up the neck.

questions.question: Which sea genius has a donut brain wrapped around its throat pipe?
questions.note: An octopus esophagus passes through a ring-like central brain area.

questions.question: Which microscopic tank can endure the vacuum of space in hibernation mode?
questions.note: Tardigrades survive extremes via cryptobiosis.

questions.question: Which fruit wears its tiny seed-specks on the outside like sequins?
questions.note: Its exterior achenes each contain a seed.

questions.question: Which two star colors do we not naturally see as pure stellar colors?
questions.note: Star spectra and perception make pure green or purple stars absent.

questions.question: Which country wins many per-capita chocolate speedrun leaderboards?
questions.note: Switzerland often ranks very high in chocolate consumption per person.

questions.question: Which snack tube doubled as an urn in a famously crunchy farewell?
questions.note: Inventor Fred Baur had part of his ashes buried in one.

questions.question: Which painter became a superstar after mostly being ignored while alive?
questions.note: Van Gogh sold very few paintings in his lifetime.

questions.question: Which moon is an ice geyser chaos orb spraying water into space?
questions.note: Enceladus ejects plumes that feed Saturn's E ring.

questions.question: Which planet rolls around the Sun like a tipped-over bowling pin?
questions.note: Uranus has an axial tilt of about 98 degrees.

questions.question: What smell do astronauts report on suits after a spacewalk, like cosmic barbecue?
questions.note: Astronauts describe a metallic or seared smell after EVA.

questions.question: Which continent is so extreme that native ants basically said
questions.note: Ants are native to every continent except Antarctica.

questions.question: Which language can answer yes/no questions without separate words for yes or no?
questions.note: Irish often answers by repeating or negating the verb.

questions.question: Which city hosts a wall intentionally marinated in decades of chewing gum?
questions.note: Seattle's Gum Wall is a famous sticky landmark.

questions.question: Which island nation lives with zero permanent rivers and lakes?
questions.note: Malta has no permanent rivers or lakes.

questions.question: Which mammal can pause pregnancy like biology hit the snooze button?
questions.note: Some kangaroos use embryonic diapause to delay development.

questions.question: Which bird lays an egg so giant it feels proportionally illegal?
questions.note: A kiwi egg can be around one-fifth of female body mass.

questions.question: Which fruit can sting your mouth because it contains microscopic needles?
questions.note: Raphides and bromelain contribute to pineapple mouth-tingle.

questions.question: Which US state slogan sounds like a futuristic expedition game objective?
questions.note: Its motto is

questions.question: Which ingredient gave Roman marine concrete its legendary stubbornness?
questions.note: Pozzolanic reactions improved long-term durability, even in seawater.

questions.question: Which tiny worker can carry loads many times heavier than itself?
questions.note: Leafcutter ants can carry several multiples of body weight.

questions.question: Which weather trick can lead to fish apparently raining from the sky?
questions.note: Strong vortices can lift small aquatic animals and drop them inland.

questions.question: Which ancient engineer described a coin-operated holy-water dispenser, proto-vending style?
questions.note: Hero documented mechanisms that dispensed liquid for a coin.

questions.question: Which nut naturally pops its shell seam like a tiny green grin?
questions.note: Ripe pistachio shells usually split open naturally.

questions.question: Which Arctic giant has a built-in transparent eyelid for snow and swim mode?
questions.note: Polar bears have a nictitating membrane for eye protection.

questions.question: Which fish can flop-walk on mud and climb mangrove roots?
questions.note: Mudskippers are amphibious fish adapted for land movement.

questions.question: Which shrimp sees color with hardware that makes human eyes look budget-tier?
questions.note: Mantis shrimp have very complex photoreceptor systems.

questions.question: Which deep-sea giant hides a parrot-like beak in arm-noodle central?
questions.note: Giant squid use a hard beak to tear prey.

questions.question: Which London icon name belongs to a bell, not the tower tourists point at?
questions.note: Big Ben originally names the Great Bell inside the tower.

questions.question: Which city was once attacked by an actual wave of molasses?
questions.note: A 1919 molasses tank burst caused a deadly flood.

questions.question: Which soda began life as a pharmacy tonic before becoming a fridge staple?
questions.note: Dr Pepper originated in a drugstore setting.

questions.question: Which orchestra instrument used
strings mostly made from sheep intestines?
questions.note: Traditional catgut strings were usually sheep or goat intestine.

questions.question: Which moon has methane rain and hydrocarbon lakes like alien weather DLC?
questions.note: Titan has a methane-based weather cycle.

questions.question: Which country has the largest stash of natural lakes on Earth?
questions.note: Canada contains a huge share of the world's lakes.

questions.question: Which extinct bird had a wingspan wide enough to embarrass small airplanes?
questions.note: Argentavis is estimated among the largest flying birds ever.

questions.question: Which frog can freeze partly solid in winter then reboot in spring?
questions.note: Wood frogs survive freezing using cryoprotective biochemistry.

questions.question: Which ancient monument keeps surviving by receiving replacement stone patchwork?
questions.note: The Sphinx has undergone extensive repair and block replacement.

questions.question: Which bird can imitate camera shutters, alarms, and chainsaws like an audio prankster?
questions.note: Lyrebirds are exceptional vocal mimics of natural and human sounds.

questions.question: Which armored marine relic has blue blood used in medical testing?
questions.note: Horseshoe crab blood is blue due to hemocyanin.

questions.question: Which bird builds decorated dating stages and collects colorful trinkets?
questions.note: Male bowerbirds build and decorate bowers to attract mates.

questions.question: Which stone often preserves fossil textures after mineral replacement over ages?
questions.note: Silicification can preserve biological structures in agate-like forms.

questions.question: Which tiny mammal has such a turbo metabolism it must eat almost constantly?
questions.note: Many shrews need frequent feeding due to high metabolic rates.

questions.question: Which marine reptile can stretch dives by dramatically slowing heart rate?
questions.note: Sea turtles conserve oxygen during deep or long dives.

questions.question: Which giant bloom smells like a villainous compost heap to attract pollinators?
questions.note: Amorphophallus titanum emits carrion-like odor when flowering.

questions.question: Which river-engineer rodent can stay underwater for over 15 minutes?
questions.note: Beavers are adapted for long submersion while swimming and working.

questions.question: Which famously mocked font was made for comic-style software speech bubbles?
questions.note: Comic Sans was created by Vincent Connare for Microsoft.

questions.question: Which instrument is played by waving your hands through invisible electric fields?
questions.note: Theremin pitch and volume are controlled without physical contact.

questions.question: Which birds can sleep with half their brain awake during travel?
questions.note: Unihemispheric sleep enables partial rest during vigilance.

questions.question: Which huge mammal can produce milk that appears pinkish under some conditions?
questions.note: Hippo milk can look pink due to secretions and optical effects.

questions.question: Which country created a government role specifically targeting loneliness?
questions.note: The UK established a Minister for Loneliness role.

questions.question: Which small fish can live out of water for extended periods in damp habitat?
questions.note: Mangrove killifish can survive on land in moist conditions.

questions.question: Which living bird owns the current wingspan world record?
questions.note: Wandering albatross wingspans can exceed 3.5 meters.

questions.question: Which mega-city uncovered and restored an urban stream as flood-control and public space?
questions.note: The Cheonggyecheon restoration transformed central Seoul infrastructure.

questions.question: Which shark body surface is basically covered in microscopic teeth?
questions.note: Dermal denticles reduce drag and protect skin.

questions.question: Which tropical fruit evolved to ocean-drift like a self-seeding raft capsule?
questions.note: Fibrous husks and buoyancy aid long-distance sea dispersal.

questions.question: Which board game is older than chess and still deeply alive today?
questions.note: Go originated in ancient China over two millennia ago.

questions.question: Which giant marine reptile is wrongly called a dinosaur in pop culture?
questions.note: Mosasaurs were marine squamates, not dinosaurs.

questions.question: Which tree became famous in ecology lore for a debated dodo-linked germination story?
questions.note: The classic dodo-only germination claim is famous but disputed.

questions.question: Which Atlantic heat conveyor keeps Western Europe milder than latitude twins elsewhere?
questions.note: North Atlantic circulation transports warm water and influences climate.

questions.question: Which human body part stays clear partly by having no blood vessels at all?
questions.note: The cornea is avascular and gets oxygen from air and tears.

questions.question: Which bird earns a
name by dropping skeleton snacks from heights?
questions.note: Bearded vultures break bones by dropping them onto rocks.

questions.question: Which constellation includes a famous red supergiant nearing its stellar finale?
questions.note: Betelgeuse in Orion is a red supergiant late in its evolution.

questions.question: Which snow-loving microalga paints mountainsides pink as
questions.note: Blooms of this alga can color snow red-pink.

questions.question: Which jelly dessert ingredient comes from boiled red seaweed instead of animal gelatin?
questions.note: Agar is derived from red algae and used as a gelling agent.
